title: Ulyana and the Ledger
premise: August Brightwater, the meticulous archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is drawn into a murder investigation when a body is found in the locked crypt wearing clothes stolen from her own closet — and the victim's face is a stranger's, but the fingerprints are hers. As Detective Inspector Sorrel Vance works the case, August realizes the killer has been reading her private case files for years and is staging crimes from her own solved cases in reverse. The trail leads to the cathedral's foundling registry and a decades-old adoption scandal that August herself was quietly erased from. In the end, August traps the killer — her long-lost half-sibling, raised on stolen records and grievance — at the anniversary dinner by feeding them a falsified file, choosing truth over the comfortable family lie she'd built her identity on.
about_author: B. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing births, deaths, and disappearances in English cathedral towns before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people whose lives are filed away in someone else's drawers.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: August Brightwater's POV. August opens the crypt for its annual inspection and finds it sealed from inside — yet a body lies within, dressed in clothes she recognizes as her own. The emotional beat is cold dread beneath professional composure; her pride in order begins to crack.

chapters.title: Clothes That Fit
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Sorrel Vance's POV. Vance catalogs the scene: the victim wears August's missing cardigan, and the fingerprints lifted match August's own. Vance must treat her witness as suspect, establishing wary mutual distrust laced with reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: Filing Errors
chapters.summary: August's POV. August audits her own archive and discovers pages razored from the foundling registry — including an entry bearing her childhood name. The beat is vertigo: the past she curated may have been edited before she ever read it.

chapters.title: The Witness Wears Grey
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Vance interviews the cathedral staff and notices one verger reciting details no outsider could know — details matching August's private case notes. Suspicion shifts toward whoever reads what August writes.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: August's POV. The cathedral prepares its 300th-anniversary dinner, a deadline now looming over everything. August, rattled, finds a photocopy of one of her closed cases tucked into her coat pocket. Beat: hunted in her own house.

chapters.title: Reverse Chronology
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Vance maps the crime against August's old case files and realizes the killer is re-enacting August's solved cases backward, most recent first. The emotional beat is grim awe — the killer isn't taunting police; they're grading August.

chapters.title: What the Registry Kept
chapters.summary: August's POV. Digging into diocesan archives, August finds evidence of a 1980s adoption scandal: babies recorded as foundlings were quietly placed with donors, paper trails rewritten. Her own record is among them. Beat: identity as something done to you.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Face
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. The victim is identified: a records clerk who once handled the foundling files. She had recently contacted the cathedral asking about 'the Brightwater entry.' Vance and August formally pool knowledge — an uneasy alliance forms.

chapters.title: The Second Costume
chapters.summary: August's POV. A near-miss: another staged tableau appears, this time using clothes belonging to Vance. August realizes the killer can reach anyone connected to the file. Beat: guilt — her archive is the weapon.

chapters.title: Brother, Unlisted
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Genealogical work surfaces a second child recorded the same night as August — a boy entered as stillborn, later alive in a donor household. Someone was raised on the lie of the ledger. Beat: the shape of a motive emerges.

chapters.title: Interlude: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Killer's POV, unnamed. Short, chilling chapter of annotations written in the margins of August's old case files — corrections, compliments, grievances. The reader sees devotion curdling into ownership. Beat: intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: The Verger's Alibi
chapters.summary: August's POV. August confronts the suspicious verger, who breaks: he was paid anonymously to copy registry pages years ago and has been terrified since. He gives her a dead-drop address. Beat: fear passed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Surveillance of the dead drop yields nothing but a note addressed to August by a childhood nickname only her family used. Vance warns August she may be the intended final exhibit. Beat: loyalty tested — protect the witness or use her as bait?

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: August's POV. Anniversary dinner planning accelerates; the guest list includes descendants of the original donors. August recognizes a name from the scandal and quietly requests the seating chart. Beat: the trap begins forming in her mind.

chapters.title: The File That Lies
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. August proposes baiting the killer with a forged case file planted where only a reader of her archive would find it. Vance resists, then relents — but insists on controlling the release. Beat: two control freaks learning trust.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: August's POV. The forged file — claiming the foundling ledger's original page survives hidden in the crypt — is seeded into the archive. August watches the reading room all day through the catalogue system. Beat: patience as suspense.

chapters.title: Someone Reads It
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. The file is accessed after hours via a stolen keycard traced to the anniversary catering staff. A face is caught on camera: a man whose features echo August's own. Beat: recognition without a name.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the anniversary dinner, toasts begin. August scans the room and finds him serving wine — her half-brother, embedded for weeks. Their eyes meet across the candlelight. Beat: terror and grief in a single held glance.

chapters.title: Crypt Reckoning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. He lures August to the crypt with the promise of the true ledger page; Vance follows the forged-file signal. Confrontation: he wanted August to find him, to be seen by the only family the records left him. Beat: climax — violence averted by truth spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Confession in Ink
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Arrest and confession: he killed the clerk who threatened to expose his existence before he could decide what to do with it, then staged everything from August's files to force her to look for him. Beat: horror braided with heartbreak.

chapters.title: Amendments
chapters.summary: August's POV. August restores the mutilated registry pages and adds a truthful amendment about her own origins, publicly, in the archive. Found family — Vance, the verger, the cathedral staff — stands beside her. Beat: identity reclaimed as chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Closing the Case
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue. Months later, August closes the file on the case she never wanted, visits her brother in prison, and locks the crypt — this time knowing exactly what it holds. Final beat: the ledger balanced, loyalty and truth finally on the same page.
